notes:
Mid-market product org (customer support workflows). Evaluating Redwood Hosted first (quick PoC in Feb) then moving to Dedicated for production. Key ask: predictable p95 latency < 300ms for short chat queries, bulk embeddings job throughput ~500 docs/min, and reranking under 200ms 90th perc for top-10 lists. Very cost sensitive vs managed alternatives; interested in batching + prefix caching suggestions. Security: strict SSO/SAML, SOC2 required, KMS for encryption, audit logs retention 13 months, and EU data residency for subset of EU customers. Quote from Head of Product: "We need consistent latency where customers notice no lag — but can't double infra costs."

POC scope: dedicated reserved pool (2x A100 equiv), canary route 10% traffic -> dedicated, 90% hosted for 2 weeks, then ramp to 100% if metrics stable. Fallback: automatic route to hosted_api in case of Dedicated capacity/backpressure or region outage; model variant fallback to a smaller quantized model for latency spikes. Rollback strategy: immediate rollback to hosted_api for >1% error rate or p95 > 500ms for >30m; manual rollback for feature regressions.

Notes style: fragments, action items, links to drive/jira. SE will run live perf run with sample prod-trace prompts. Legal requested encryption-at-rest diagram and processing locations. Budget range aligns with mid-market reserved capacity contract.

poc_summary: Dedicated POC: 4-week engagement. Objectives: validate latency SLOs (p95 < 300ms for chat), validate canary routing and automated fallback to hosted_api, prove model variant fallback for tails, and measure cost per 1K tokens under real traffic patterns. Deliverables: perf report, rollout runbook, cost model, security artifacts.
canary_plan: Week 1: deploy dedicated pool + instrument metrics. Week 2: route 10% real traffic to dedicated via canary; monitor p95, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization. Week 3: ramp 10 -> 30 -> 60% if metrics stable. Week 4: full 100% or rollback. SE to configure traffic split policy and circuit-breaker thresholds.
fallback_routing: Primary route: Dedicated (region preference: us-east). Fallback rules: capacity/latency triggers -> automatic route to Hosted API in same region; region outage -> route to closest healthy region (us-west or eu-west) with data residency tag check. Model variant fallback: full fp16 model -> quantized int8 variant when p95 latency breach persists >10m.
